profile.address: Rollins Ford Road, Linton Hall, Prince William County, VA 20156
profile.reading:
This building is part of Google's Northern Virginia data center footprint, mapped near Linton Hall along Rollins Ford Road in Prince William County, the site of the third Google facility the company opened in the Northern Virginia region in 2023. Google's own Virginia locations page, fetched this session, does not name individual buildings or addresses within its Northern Virginia footprint, so this specific structure is not independently identified beyond its OSM-derived location.

Google's cloud infrastructure operates as a business of Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL/GOOG, SEC CIK 0001652044), headquartered at 1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, California. Google's own Virginia data center location page, fetched fresh this session, states the company established a Virginia presence in 2009, purchased Northern Virginia land in 2017, opened its first facility in 2019, expanded a second Loudoun County facility in 2021, and opened a third in Prince William County in 2023; in 2025 Google announced a $9 billion investment for 2025-2026 spanning existing Northern Virginia sites and a new Chesterfield County campus. Google reports $15.6 billion in Virginia economic activity and over 36,000 employee volunteer hours since 2010.

Northern Virginia's Data Center Alley corridor, of which this Prince William County building is part, hosts large single-tenant campuses for AWS and Meta and colocation operators including Digital Realty and Equinix, all separately tracked in this registry, though Google's own public materials describe its Virginia footprint in aggregate rather than naming individual buildings or per-building capacity figures.

Loudoun and Prince William counties sit at the center of what industry trackers call Data Center Alley, the largest concentration of data center capacity in the world by aggregate power draw, a status Loudoun County's own economic development office has cited in public materials for over a decade. Dominion Energy, the regional utility, has repeatedly flagged this corridor in integrated resource plan filings with the Virginia State Corporation Commission as the single largest driver of new electricity demand in its Virginia service territory, prompting new transmission and generation investment. Virginia's data center sales-and-use tax exemption, administered by the Virginia Economic Development Partnership and renewed by the General Assembly, has been a material factor in Google and other hyperscalers continuing to expand in the corridor rather than building only in lower-tax states, though Google has not disclosed how much exemption value this specific facility has claimed.

reading.body:
This building sits within Google's Northern Virginia campus, which the company opened its third facility in during 2023 along Rollins Ford Road in Prince William County. Google does not publish megawatt capacity or square footage for individual buildings within its Northern Virginia footprint, disclosing instead only that it has established a presence there since 2009, purchased land in 2017, opened its first facility in 2019, expanded a second facility in Loudoun County in 2021, and in 2025 announced a $9 billion investment for 2025-2026 spanning existing Northern Virginia sites and a new Chesterfield County campus. The specific power draw and rack density of this structure are not published.

Northern Virginia hosts the world's largest concentration of data center capacity by aggregate power draw, anchored by the Loudoun County corridor known as Data Center Alley, where this Prince William County building sits alongside large single-tenant campuses operated by AWS and Meta and colocation providers including Digital Realty and Equinix. Dominion Energy, the regional utility, has identified data center demand as the fastest growing category on its Virginia system in integrated resource plan filings with the state regulator. Virginia's sales-and-use tax exemption for qualifying data center equipment, administered by the Virginia Economic Development Partnership, applies to facilities meeting the state's criteria.

Google's Northern Virginia footprint is not ranked among Virginia's 23 mapped facilities with published megawatt figures, which together total 1,375 megawatts across 326 mapped sites statewide. The absence of a published capacity figure for this Prince William County building means its contribution to the state's total capacity and its significance relative to other facilities cannot be derived from operator disclosures. A county assessor parcel lookup would be required to establish building-specific square footage and to assess the site's scale within Google's regional footprint.
